blogPosts.title: How Much Does Water Heater Replacement Cost in Denver in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about water heater replacement costs in Denver? We break down pricing factors, equipment options, and what to expect from a professional installation.
body: Replacing a water heater is one of the most significant plumbing investments a Denver homeowner will make, and understanding the costs upfront helps you plan with confidence. In the Denver metro area, water heater replacement typically ranges from $1,200 to $4,500 depending on the type of unit, its capacity, and the complexity of the installation. At My Purple Plumber, we have installed hundreds of water heaters across Denver neighborhoods from Washington Park to Highlands, and we always provide a detailed, upfront quote before any work begins. The key cost factors include the unit itself, labor, any necessary plumbing modifications, and whether you are switching from a tank to a tankless system.

Tank water heaters remain the most common choice for Denver homes, typically costing between $1,200 and $2,500 installed for a standard 40 to 50-gallon unit. These systems are straightforward to install and work well for most households of two to four people. Gas tank models tend to be slightly more expensive to install due to venting requirements, but they cost less to operate over time — an important consideration given Denver's cold winters when your water heater works overtime. Our Denver plumbing team will help you choose the right tank size and fuel type for your home's specific needs and your monthly budget.

Tankless water heaters have become increasingly popular among Denver homeowners looking to save space and reduce energy costs. These on-demand systems heat water only when you need it, eliminating the standby energy loss of traditional tank models. In Denver, tankless water heater installation typically costs between $2,500 and $4,500, depending on the unit's capacity and whether your home's gas line and venting need upgrades. While the upfront investment is higher, tankless units can last 20 years or more — roughly double the lifespan of a standard tank — and can reduce your water heating costs by 30 to 40 percent annually.

Denver's altitude and climate also play a role in water heater performance and replacement timing. At 5,280 feet above sea level, gas-burning appliances operate differently than they do at lower elevations, which is why it is critical to have a licensed Denver plumber handle your installation. Our technicians are trained to properly adjust gas input rates and venting for high-altitude performance, ensuring your new water heater runs efficiently and safely. Additionally, Denver's cold incoming water temperatures in winter mean your unit has to work harder, making proper sizing essential for consistent hot water delivery throughout your home.

One common mistake Denver homeowners make is waiting until their water heater completely fails before replacing it. Signs that your unit is nearing the end of its life include inconsistent water temperature, rust-colored water, unusual noises from the tank, and visible corrosion on the tank or connections. If your water heater is more than 10 years old and showing any of these symptoms, it is wise to start planning for replacement before you face an emergency. My Purple Plumber offers free assessments for Denver homeowners who want to understand their options and budget before the situation becomes urgent.

At My Purple Plumber, we help Denver homeowners navigate every step of the water heater replacement process, from selecting the right unit to handling permits and final inspection. Our upfront pricing means you will never be surprised by hidden costs, and every installation comes with our workmanship guarantee. We also offer financing options for larger installations, making it easier to invest in an energy-efficient system without straining your budget. Whether you are in Stapleton, LoDo, or anywhere across the Denver metro, our team is ready to help you choose and install the perfect water heater for your home.

If you are unsure whether to repair or replace your water heater, contact My Purple Plumber today for an honest assessment. Our licensed Denver plumbers will evaluate your current unit, explain your options clearly, and provide a fixed quote so you can make an informed decision. With over 10 years of experience serving the Denver community, we have the expertise to ensure your new water heater is installed correctly, efficiently, and at a fair price. Call us at (720) 795-4699 or visit our website to schedule your free water heater consultation in Denver.

blogPosts.title: Signs Your Denver Home Needs Professional Drain Cleaning
blogPosts.excerpt: Slow drains and gurgling sounds could mean trouble. Learn the warning signs Denver homeowners should watch for before a small clog becomes a big problem.
body: Clogged drains are one of the most common plumbing issues Denver homeowners face, and while a slow-draining sink might seem minor, it can quickly escalate into a major problem if left unaddressed. At My Purple Plumber, we respond to dozens of drain cleaning calls each month across the Denver metro area, and we have seen firsthand how preventive maintenance can save homeowners hundreds or even thousands of dollars in repair costs. Understanding the warning signs that your drains need professional attention is the first step toward avoiding sewage backups, water damage, and expensive emergency repairs that could have been prevented.

The most obvious sign you need professional drain cleaning is water that drains slowly from sinks, showers, or bathtubs. While a minor clog might cause water to drain a little slower than usual, a significant blockage will cause water to pool and stand in your fixtures for extended periods. In Denver's older neighborhoods like Capitol Hill, Baker, and Highland, homes often have aging cast iron or galvanized steel pipes that are particularly prone to buildup and corrosion. If you notice slow drainage in multiple fixtures throughout your home, that usually indicates a problem in your main sewer line rather than an isolated drain clog.

Gurgling sounds coming from your drains are another red flag that should not be ignored. These sounds occur when air is trapped behind a blockage and forced through the water in your P-traps. You might hear gurgling after flushing a toilet, running the washing machine, or simply running water in the kitchen sink. In Denver, where winter temperatures regularly drop below freezing, pipe contraction and seasonal ground movement can shift underground sewer lines and create partial blockages that cause these gurgling sounds. Our Denver plumbing team uses high-definition sewer cameras to pinpoint exactly where the problem is located.

Frequent clogs in the same drain, recurring toilet backups, and unpleasant sewer odors inside your home are all signs that a simple drain snake or chemical treatment is not enough. These symptoms often point to deeper issues such as tree root intrusion, pipe scale buildup, or a collapsed section of your sewer line. Denver is known for its large cottonwood and elm trees, and their aggressive root systems frequently invade sewer lateral lines, especially in older neighborhoods. If you are experiencing repeated drain problems, a professional sewer scope inspection can identify the root cause before it leads to a complete sewer line failure.

Many Denver homeowners try to address slow drains with chemical drain cleaners from the hardware store, but these products often do more harm than good. Harsh chemical cleaners can corrode older pipes, damage rubber seals and gaskets, and only partially clear the blockage — leaving most of the buildup behind to cause problems again within weeks. Professional drain cleaning by a licensed Denver plumber uses mechanical and hydro-jetting methods that completely clear the blockage without damaging your pipes. At My Purple Plumber, we always start with a camera inspection so we can see exactly what is causing the clog and recommend the most effective solution.

Hydro-jetting is the gold standard for drain cleaning in Denver homes, especially for clearing heavy buildup, grease accumulation, and tree root intrusion. This method uses high-pressure water streams to scour the inside of your pipes clean, restoring them to near-original flow capacity. For Denver's older homes with decades of accumulated pipe scale and debris, hydro-jetting provides a more thorough and longer-lasting solution than traditional snaking. Our Denver plumbing team carries professional-grade hydro-jetting equipment on every service vehicle, so we can typically resolve your drain issues in a single visit without scheduling follow-up appointments.

The best time to address drain cleaning is before you have an emergency. Scheduling annual or bi-annual drain maintenance with a trusted Denver plumber can keep your pipes flowing freely and help you avoid the stress and expense of unexpected backups. At My Purple Plumber, we offer preventive drain cleaning services tailored to Denver homes, including camera inspections that can catch developing problems before they become full-blown emergencies. Contact us today at (720) 795-4699 to schedule a drain assessment for your Denver home and keep your plumbing system in top condition year-round.

blogPosts.title: Best Water Filtration Systems for Denver's Hard Water
blogPosts.excerpt: Denver's water contains dissolved minerals that affect taste and appliance longevity. Discover the filtration options that work best for Mile High City homes.
body: Denver's water supply is drawn from mountain snowmelt and treated at municipal facilities, but by the time it reaches your taps, it can contain significant levels of dissolved minerals, chlorine, and other contaminants that affect both taste and household appliances. Hard water — water with high concentrations of calcium and magnesium — is a common issue throughout the Denver metro area, and it can cause everything from chalky buildup on fixtures to reduced efficiency in your water heater and dishwasher. Understanding your water quality and choosing the right filtration system is an investment that pays dividends in both comfort and long-term savings for Denver homeowners.

The first step in selecting a water filtration system for your Denver home is understanding what is actually in your water. Denver Water, the primary municipal provider, publishes annual water quality reports that detail the mineral content, treatment chemicals, and potential contaminants in the supply. However, the condition of your home's internal plumbing can also affect water quality, especially in older Denver homes with aging pipes. My Purple Plumber offers water testing services that analyze your home's actual water at the tap, giving you a clear picture of what filtration solutions will be most effective for your specific situation.

Point-of-use filtration systems are an affordable and effective option for Denver homeowners who want cleaner drinking water without investing in a whole-home solution. Reverse osmosis systems installed under your kitchen sink can remove up to 99 percent of dissolved contaminants, including lead, fluoride, nitrates, and chlorine, producing clean, great-tasting water for drinking and cooking. These systems typically cost between $300 and $800 installed in Denver, making them accessible for most households. Our Denver plumbing team installs reverse osmosis systems from top manufacturers and can help you choose the right unit based on your water quality test results.

Whole-home water filtration systems take things a step further by treating all the water entering your Denver home, not just the water at a single tap. These systems are particularly beneficial for homes with hard water issues, as they can include water softening technology that prevents mineral buildup in your pipes, water heater, and appliances. For Denver homeowners, whole-home filtration systems typically range from $1,500 to $4,000 depending on the system type and your home's plumbing configuration. While the upfront investment is significant, the long-term savings on appliance repairs, reduced soap and detergent usage, and improved water quality make these systems a smart choice.

Denver's high altitude and dry climate also create unique water quality considerations. The low humidity means evaporative coolers are common throughout the metro area, and the minerals in hard water can cause significant scaling in these systems, reducing their efficiency and lifespan. Additionally, Denver homeowners who garden or landscape often find that hard water affects plant health and soil quality over time. A water softener or filtration system can address these concerns by removing excess minerals before they cause problems throughout your home. Our team at My Purple Plumber can assess your home's water quality and recommend the right combination of filtration technologies.

Carbon filtration systems offer another popular option for Denver homes, providing excellent removal of chlorine, volatile organic compounds, and unpleasant tastes and odors. These systems are often more affordable than reverse osmosis units and do not produce wastewater, making them an environmentally friendly choice. For Denver families who want better-tasting water for drinking and cooking without the complexity of a reverse osmosis system, a high-quality carbon filter installed by a licensed Denver plumber can make a noticeable difference. We can install carbon filtration at the point of entry to treat all your home's water or at specific points of use for targeted filtration.

Choosing the right water filtration system for your Denver home does not have to be overwhelming. At My Purple Plumber, we start every filtration project with a thorough water quality assessment and a straightforward conversation about your goals and budget. Whether you want cleaner drinking water, protection for your appliances, or a comprehensive whole-home solution, our Denver plumbing team will design and install a system that meets your needs. Contact us at (720) 795-4699 to schedule a water quality test and learn how a filtration system can improve your Denver home's water quality today.

blogPosts.title: What to Do in a Plumbing Emergency: A Denver Homeowner's Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A burst pipe or overflowing toilet can cause thousands in damage. Here is what Denver homeowners should do immediately before the plumber arrives.
body: A plumbing emergency can strike at any time — a burst pipe at 2 AM, a backed-up sewer on a holiday weekend, or a water heater failure in the middle of January when Denver temperatures plunge well below freezing. Knowing what to do in those critical first minutes can mean the difference between a minor inconvenience and thousands of dollars in water damage. At My Purple Plumber, we respond to emergency calls across the Denver metro area every day, and we have put together this guide to help Denver homeowners take immediate action while waiting for professional help to arrive.

The first and most important step in any plumbing emergency is to shut off the water supply to prevent further damage. Every Denver homeowner should know where their main water shut-off valve is located — it is typically near the water meter, in the basement, or on an exterior wall facing the street. In an emergency, turn this valve clockwise to stop water flow to your entire home. If you only have a problem with a specific fixture, look for individual shut-off valves behind toilets or under sinks. Keeping a wrench near your main shut-off valve ensures you can turn it even if the handle is stiff or corroded.

Once you have shut off the water, the next priority is protecting your property from water damage. Move furniture, electronics, and valuables away from the affected area. Place buckets under active leaks and use towels or rags to absorb standing water. If water has reached electrical outlets or appliances, do not touch them and turn off the electricity at the breaker panel immediately. Denver homes with basements are particularly vulnerable to water damage during plumbing emergencies, as water naturally flows downward and can quickly flood lower levels. Quick action in these first minutes can save you thousands in restoration costs.

For burst pipes, which are a particular risk during Denver's harsh winter months, time is critical. When temperatures drop below zero, the water inside exposed or poorly insulated pipes can freeze and expand with enough force to crack copper, PVC, and even steel pipes. If you discover a burst pipe, shut off the main water supply immediately and open all faucets to drain the remaining water from the system. This reduces the amount of water that can leak from the break. Keep the affected area as warm as possible by closing doors to the damaged room and using space heaters if safe to do so.

A backed-up sewer line is another common emergency that requires immediate professional attention. If multiple drains in your Denver home are backing up simultaneously or you notice sewage coming up through floor drains, this is almost certainly a main sewer line blockage. Avoid using any water in your home until a plumber can assess the situation, as additional water will only worsen the backup. Sewage exposure poses serious health risks, so keep children and pets away from affected areas. Denver's older neighborhoods are especially susceptible to sewer backups due to aging clay and cast iron lateral lines.

When calling an emergency plumber in Denver, be prepared to describe your situation clearly. Let the dispatcher know what happened, whether you have shut off the water, the extent of any flooding, and whether there are any immediate safety concerns like gas smells or electrical hazards. At My Purple Plumber, our emergency response team is available seven days a week and we prioritize calls based on urgency. We keep our service vehicles fully stocked with the most common parts and equipment, which allows us to resolve the majority of emergency repairs in a single visit.

The best way to handle a plumbing emergency is to prevent one from happening in the first place. Regular plumbing maintenance, including annual inspections, water heater servicing, and drain cleaning, can catch developing problems before they become emergencies. Denver homeowners who invest in preventive plumbing care experience fewer unexpected breakdowns and lower overall repair costs. My Purple Plumber offers comprehensive plumbing maintenance plans for Denver homes that include priority scheduling, discounted emergency rates, and thorough system inspections. Contact us at (720) 795-4699 to set up a maintenance plan and give yourself peace of mind year-round.
